uncertainty: Twelve pinned open-source C API package paths passed the valid one-page local PDF control and returned a parsed page count: Poppler GLib, qpdf C API, MuPDF, Ghostscript, PDFio, PDFium, Vanilla.PDF, tspdf, ImageMagick, GraphicsMagick, libvips, and pdf_oxide. qpdf C API is compiled as C and linked with C++ as its official library documentation requires; its underlying engine is C++. The Poppler GLib frontend shares the Poppler core used in the C++ PDF cell. PDFio is source-built. PDFium uses a SHA-256-pinned macOS arm64 distributor binary and an original public header matched to canonical source revision 6688c576fd851f4159c6fae39396da50939de110; this does not prove every binary source file equals that revision. Apple Core Graphics is separately verified as a macOS platform runtime API. Eight more third-party paths are needed for the 20-path working goal. Homebrew formula-name searches returned exact windows of [38, 2, 4, 1] hits (45 total; 41 unique); these are fuzzy discovery leads, not proof or usage rankings. Homebrew is not an exhaustive C package registry. One plausible C wrapper lead remains unresolved. ImageMagick, libvips, qpdf, PDFio, Vanilla.PDF, and tspdf have exact primary GitHub star counts; the other five have canonical non-GitHub upstreams and remain unranked. ISO C standard library has no documented PDF parser. The control covers one simple unencrypted PDF only. No malformed-input, vulnerability, or resource-use experiments were run. Vanilla.PDF uses publisher NuGet C headers and native macOS arm64 runtime pinned by SHA-256; its C document header matches the tagged source, while byte-for-byte binary source provenance remains unestablished. tspdf 0.5.1 is source-built and provides a documented C11 local-file reader and page API, also used from C++17; its primary repository had zero observed stars, so there is no demonstrated adoption beyond the published release and this control. ImageMagick 7.1.2-35 and GraphicsMagick 1.3.49 read and render the local PDF through their documented C Wand APIs, reporting one 612×792 page. Their pinned PDF coder modules use installed Ghostscript 10.08.0 for PDF interpretation, so these are separate package input paths sharing Ghostscript, not independent PDF syntax engines. GraphicsMagick is canonical Mercurial and remains unranked by primary GitHub stars. libvips 8.18.7 C vips_pdfload returned PDF page count and first page dimensions; its hash-pinned vips-poppler module links the separately verified Poppler GLib engine and does not add an independent PDF syntax parser. Pixel rendering is lazy and was not exercised. pdf_oxide 0.3.78 C ABI exposes a local PDF open and parsed page count over its Rust engine; the publisher macOS arm64 binary is hash pinned and its CI-absolute install name is changed reproducibly before linking. The valid control returned one page. Source-to-binary equivalence and PDF-specific adoption remain uncertain.
